const int yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    // Clamp only at the global domain faces; interior slab faces read ghost planes\n    const int zp = (p == q.lz - 1 && q.upperEdge) ? p : p + 1;\n    const int   2.0 * center) / (q.dx * q.dx);\n    const double cyy = (f[cellIndex(q, x, yp, p)] + f[cellIndex(q, x, yn, p)] -\n                        2.0 * center) / (q.dy * q.dy);\n    const double czz = (f[cellIndex(q, x, y, zp)] + f[cellIndex(q, x, y, zn)] -\n                        2.0 * center) / (q.dz * q.dz);\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential on local planes (rank == 0);\n\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line nx;\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n        printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Compute Laplacian with clamped boundary conditions\ndouble computeLaplacian(const std::vector<double>& c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                        const double dx, const double dy, const double dz, const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z) {\n    const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n    const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n    \n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (c[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dz * dz);\n    \n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential\nvoid computeChemicalPotential(const std::vector<double>& c, std::vector<double>& mu,\n                              const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                              const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                              const double gamma, const double e_AA, const double e_BB, const double e_AB) {\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                const double cv = c[idx];\n                \n                mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB) \n                         + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                         - gamma * computeLaplacian(c, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update step\nvoid cahnHilliardUpdate(std::vector<double>& cnew, const std::vector<double>& cold,\n                        const std::vector<double>& mu,\n                        const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                        const double D, const double dt, const double dx, const double dy, const double dz) {\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                cnew[idx] = cold[idx] + dt * D * \n                           computeLaplacian(mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Initialize concentration field\nvoid initializeConcentration(std::vector<double>& c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                // Generate pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n                const size_t linear_id = z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        if (std::isnan(val) || std::isinf(val)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Check if values are in reasonable range for concentration field\n    // After Cahn-Hilliard evolution, values should typically remain bounded\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, val);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, val);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n    \n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of time steps (default: 20)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n    \n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n    \n    size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    // Allocate arrays\n    std::vector<double> cold(gridSize);\n    std::vector<double> cnew(gridSize);\n    std::vector<double> mu(gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize concentration field\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n    initializeConcentration(cold, nx, ny, nz);\n    \n    // Run simulation\n    printf(\"Running Cahn-Hilliard simulation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    for (int t = 0; t < iterations; ++t) {\n        // Compute chemical potential\n        computeChemicalPotential(cold, mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, \n                                gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB);\n        \n        // Update concentration\n        cahnHilliardUpdate(cnew, cold, mu, nx, ny, nz, D, dt, dx, dy, dz);\n        \n        // Swap buffers\n        std::swap(cold, cnew);\n    }\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzxMkVxNUYKsjtSLtZ95","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs as a hybrid MPI + CUDA + OpenMP program. It produces bit-identical results to the original and scales to 4 GPUs. Only `cahn_hilliard.cpp` and `CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable name is still `cahn_hilliard`, and no new files were added to the project.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** the grid is split into z-slabs, one rank per GPU, with ranks bound round-robin to node-local devices. A rank count above `nz/2` leaves the extra ranks idle, so every slab keeps at least two planes for halo sends.\n- **CUDA:** each rank keeps its fields on the GPU with two ghost planes per side. One halo exchange per step is enough, because `mu` is evaluated one plane past the slab. The exchange is host-staged through pinned buffers, so it doesn't require CUDA-aware MPI.\n- **Overlap:** the interior `mu` and update kernels run on a compute stream while the halo exchange runs on the host, then the boundary planes run once the ghost data has arrived.\n- **OpenMP:** initialization of the concentration field is parallelized across host threads. The main compute is GPU-bound, so OpenMP's role here is small.\n- **Output:** the full field is gathered to rank 0 only when `-r` or `-v` needs it. Output, validation, and exit codes are printed from rank 0 only, as in the original.\n- **CMake:** the `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via `LANGUAGE CUDA`, which avoids a new `.cu` file. MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA are all `REQUIRED`. The architecture list defaults to 70–90 and can be overridden.\n\n**Choices you may want to revisit**\n- **`-fmad=false`:** I added this so the GPU results match the original's unfused arithmetic exactly. Without it, nvcc fuses multiply-adds and results differ at about 1e-16. This costs about 7% on the 512³ run.\n- **Reference build:** the original built with GCC's default FMA contraction gives different hashes from both versions. I compared against the original built with `-ffp-contract=off`, which is the reference for the unfused arithmetic.\n\n**Verification**\n- Hashes and sample values match the reference exactly for 1–4 ranks. The cases cover cubic and anisotropic grids, 2-plane and 1-plane slabs, idle ranks, and zero iterations.\n- Fifteen repeated 4-rank runs gave identical hashes, so I saw no run-to-run variation.\n- `-v` exit codes, `-h`, and unknown-option handling match the original.\n- Scaling at 512³ with 100 steps: 3,091 MCUPS on 1 GPU, 6,005 on 2, and 10,412 on 4 (about 70% efficiency at 4 GPUs). The original single-threaded CPU run is about 154 MCUPS at 256³.\n\n**Not verified**\n- `compute-sanitizer` can't load its injection library in this environment, so I couldn't run memcheck or racecheck. The bit-exact repeated runs are the substitute.\n- I only tested on one 4-GPU node, not on a multi-node cluster."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":813,"cache_read_input_tokens":111659,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":813},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e35e19ad-19be-4759-aeec-3e7279974dee","uuid":"8743c5e2-4996-4801-812a-c9dd791f5f32","timestamp":"2026-10-13T21:35:22.685Z","request_id":"req_011CfzxMjzvof4CHa5cJcq4K"}
